title: Prefetch shepherd: queue oscillation dampener and soft-preempt heuristic
author: Asha Kumar
release_notes: Introduce a prefetch shepherd and soft-preempt heuristic to reduce queue oscillations and KV-prefetch-induced starvation; improves P95/P99 tail latency under mixed workloads and reduces unnecessary KV churn.
description: Context & motivation: We observed intermittent queue oscillations on high-multiplexing nodes when background KV prefetch and aggressive warmup interacted with continuous batching. Oscillations manifest as alternating micro-windows of very low latency throughput and transient starvation that inflates P99 by up to 2-3x on realistic customer workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to three interacting behaviors: (1) eager prefetch floods the KV subsystem and forces hot entries out of small, per-shard caches; (2) the batcher admission logic aggressively extends linger for expected prefetch hits which increases queue depth variance; (3) kernels that benefit from long KV warmup get starved during short bursts because of naive slot assignment. Goal: reduce queue depth oscillation, preserve KV hotness for latency-sensitive cohorts, and keep throughput/cost roughly neutral. Change summary: - Add a "prefetch shepherd" module that mediates prefetch issuance per shard and per-cohort. The shepherd enforces an elastic window: prefetches are rate-limited by a moving token budget and retractable when queue jitter exceeds thresholds. - Introduce a soft-preempt heuristic in the scheduler: long-running or KV-heavy pending requests can be gently deprioritized (not force-killed) by reducing their admission weight and nudging them into background lanes if their projected token/time cost exceeds dynamic lane budgets. - Cohort tagging for fairness: requests inherit cohort tags (interactive vs background vs offline) propagated from API layer; scheduler uses token-weighted aging to prevent starvation of low-token interactive requests. - Adaptive linger clamp: continuous-batcher linger bounds are tightened dynamically when oscillation score (a short-timescale queue variance metric) rises above a tunable threshold. - KV cache hints: add a small API to annotate prefetches with hotness score so runtime can prefer keeping high-hotness entries pinned during pressure windows. - Tests & telemetry: add end-to-end canary harness, microbenchmarks for queue jitter, and dashboards for shepherd metrics (prefetch_issued, prefetch_retracted, oscillation_score). Implementation notes (single-line summaries of commits): - commit 1: introduce prefetch_shepherd abstraction and token-bucket enforcement - commit 2: scheduler: soft-preempt heuristic, cohort-aware admission weights - commit 3: continuous-batcher: adaptive linger clamp and oscillation scoring - commit 4: kv-cache: hotness hint plumbing and pin/unpin fast path - commit 5: tests: canary scenarios, unit tests for token budgets - commit 6: docs and console telemetry wiring Checklist (what I did): - [x] Reproduced oscillation in perf-lab with mixed latency/throughput traces - [x] Designed shepherd token budget parameters and default values with simulation harness - [x] Implemented shepherd and scheduler changes with feature flag runtime.prefetch_shepherd.enabled - [x] Added unit and integration tests (batcher + kv-cache mocks) - [x] Ran cluster-scale canary (10 nodes) for 48 hours with CanaryA workload - [x] Added console panels for oscillation_score, prefetch_retracted, cohort_starvation_alerts What I measured: - CanaryA (mixed interactive + background): P95 improved from 220ms -> 160ms (~27%); P99 improved from 480ms -> 320ms (~33%) under 80% load. - Oscillation_score metric median dropped 3.8x in canary. - Prefetch issuance reduced by ~42%, while overall throughput kept within +/-2% (no throughput regression). - KV cache hit-rate for interactive cohort rose by ~9% during pressure phases. CI & review history (single contiguous timeline): Initial push (2026-01-15) wired shepherd and scheduler changes; CI: unit tests passed, integration tests failed (race in batcher_test::linger_clamp_race) — reproduced locally, added mutex and retry backoff (commit 2). Second run (2026-01-17) CI reported flaky e2e failure in canary harness due to test timeout; increased harness timeouts and trimmed logging; reran. Third run (2026-01-18) full CI passed. Reviewer feedback: - Miguel: asked for clearer invariants on token bucket deficit handling; I added docs and an invariant check in debug builds. - Lena: requested explicit safety net to disable prefetch shepherd on dedicated nodes serving legacy tenants; added runtime flag and a gate in the private deployment manifest. - Ravi: suggested adding a microbenchmark that stresses KV eviction; added kv_eviction_stress test in perf-lab. Approvals: Miguel approved (LGTM), Lena approved after private-deploy gate, Ravi approved after perf stats. Merge: squashed and merged to main (squash merge) on 2026-01-20. Runtime flags & rollout plan: - feature flag runtime.prefetch_shepherd.enabled defaults to false in telemetry regions. - Canary rollout: enable on 10% of host pools for 24h, watch oscillation_score and cohort_starvation_alerts. - Automatic rollback: if P99 regresses by >10% for interactive cohort, shepherd is disabled automatically for that pool. Files changed (high-level): - runtime/batcher/continuous_batcher.cc - runtime/scheduler/soft_preempt.cc - runtime/kv_cache/prefetch_shepherd.cc - runtime/kv_cache/hotness_hint.h - infra/canary/canary_scenarios/prefetch_shepherd.yaml - tests/perf/kv_eviction_stress_test.cc - docs/dev-notes/prefetch_shepherd.md Small illustrative snippet (from soft_preempt.cc): "// gently reduce admission weight for large projected-token requests; do not hard-preempt to preserve correctness" Testing notes & follow-ups: - Follow-up ENG-4210: tune default token-budget per-hardware-profile (A100 vs H100) — currently set conservatively. - Follow-up ENG-4265: explore hardware-assisted KV pinning APIs with partners. - Observability: Add an alert that fires when prefetch_retracted spikes > 5x baseline; instrumentation added in this PR but alert window TBD. Risk assessment and mitigation: - Risk: misconfigured token budgets could starve throughput-heavy workloads. Mitigation: feature-flagged + gradual rollout + automatic rollback rule. - Risk: increased latency for background batch jobs; mitigation: cohort tagging ensures background lanes are deprioritized but not dropped. TL;DR: Adds a runtime "prefetch shepherd" and soft-preempt scheduler logic to reduce queue oscillations and KV churn; net effect in canary: substantial P99/P95 tail latency reductions with no throughput regression.
